purpose: Test whether the staged-release invariant that survived the RC35 finite model also survives two fixed leader-termination points and loss of quorum in a real three-process etcd implementation on one host.

exploratoryRun.role: Used to correct etcdctl transaction framing and process-exit handling; it is not the confirmatory result.

fixedTopology.freshStart: The run directory is removed only after its absolute path is verified to be below .cache/rc35-etcd, then three new member directories are created.

fixedProtocol: Two clients concurrently compare version(stage)=0 and only the winning transaction writes CLAIMED plus owner.
A second compare-and-swap changes CLAIMED to RECEIPTED and writes the receipt digest in the same transaction.
A third compare-and-swap changes RECEIPTED to RELEASED and writes the outcome digest in the same transaction.

The coordinator discards the successful release response as a client observation, retries the same transition, and requires the retry to take the failure branch that returns RELEASED, receipt, and outcome.
The two cases differ only in whether the current leader is terminated immediately after CLAIMED or immediately after RECEIPTED.
After both recovery cases, two members are stopped and the remaining member attempts a new transaction; after healing, that key must be absent.

primaryCriteria.C1: Exactly one of two concurrent claim transactions succeeds in each leader-termination case.
primaryCriteria.C2: The receipt and release transitions succeed after leader replacement at both termination points.
primaryCriteria.C3: After the stopped leader restarts, all three individual linearizable reads return stage RELEASED at version 3, one receipt digest at version 1, and one outcome digest at version 1.
primaryCriteria.C4: A retry after the deliberately unavailable success response does not execute the success branch and returns the committed stage, receipt, and outcome.
primaryCriteria.C5: The single surviving minority cannot complete a write within the fixed timeout and the attempted key is absent after quorum is restored.
primaryCriteria.C6: The independent Python auditor reconstructs transaction order and all five substantive criteria directly from the persisted command history and passes every fixed check.

failureRule: Any failed C1-C6 criterion makes the confirmatory run non-qualifying. No post-run threshold, event ordering, key version, or digest change is allowed.
stopRule: Stop and retain the failure record if the official archive digest differs, the fresh cluster cannot become healthy within 30 seconds, a process cannot be terminated, a transaction violates stage order, or the minority attempt commits.

claimBoundary.maySupport: The concrete compare-and-swap construction tolerates the two tested leader process terminations and refuses the tested one-member minority write on one Windows host.
mayNotSupport: a real network partition, delay distribution, packet duplication, or packet reordering
exactly-once delivery to an external recipient

nextRungIfQualified: Run the same fixed history schema on three independent hosts with a controllable network partition and an external outcome sink that records delivery separately from committed state.
